why: Doc quote and identifier both check out; the CONSEQUENCE is false, which is this repo's documented recurring false positive (inert-worklist section 4, shape 3: 'enforcement one layer up'). (1) VERBATIM: admin-setup.md:97 is the table row '| [Version floor](/docs/en/settings) | Prevent auto-update from installing below an org-wide minimum | `minimumVersion` |'. Whole line read, nothing reverses it; :98 confirms requiredMinimumVersion is the stronger sibling. (2) IDENTIFIER: managed-version-gate.ts:12 does say 'Differs from `minimumVersion`, which prevents downgrades but never blocks startup', and MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS (managed-policy.ts:501-534) carries requiredMinimumVersion/requiredMaximumVersion and no `minimumVersion`. `grep -rna minimumVersion` over the repo finds no reader anywhere except that one comment. Both required* keys ARE enforced, on both surfaces: apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:1102 and packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/headless-start.ts:645 both call assertManagedVersionAllowed (headless-start.ts:117). (3) CONSEQUENCE 'a managed fleet with an auto-update feed has no floor on what the updater may install' is FALSE. The updater is electron-updater 6.8.9 (apps/electron/src/main/auto-update.ts). `allowDowngrade` is left at its default false (node_modules/electron-updater/out/AppUpdater.js:138) and `autoUpdater.channel` is never assigned anywhere in apps/electron/src -- the channel setter (AppUpdater.js:44) is the only thing that would silently flip allowDowngrade to true. AppUpdater.js:362 returns `this.allowDowngrade && isLatestVersionOlder`, so a feed entry below the running version is rejected outright, logged at :405 as 'downgrade is disallowed'. There IS a floor on what the updater may install, it is hard, and it cannot be lowered by a user: the currently-running version. (4) The scenario the setting exists for cannot arise here. settings.md:294 defines minimumVersion as the pin created when a user switches from the `latest` channel to `stable` via /config and elects to stay put ('Choosing to stay sets this value'), with managed use as a secondary note. Our update channel is baked into app-update.yml at build time from NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_CHANNEL (apps/electron/electron-builder.yml:80); there is no runtime channel switcher and no `claude update <version>` equivalent, so no in-product path can request an older version in the first place. Not one of the nine inert-worklist section 3 owner decisions (checked; they cover the seatbelt wildcard, availableModels, classifyAllShell, delivery drops, hooks-runtime, SdkMcpServerConfig.required and three session-mirror rows). Note also that the plans' earlier answer at 2026-07-28-managed-policy-tolerance.md:302 ('We carry none') is stale for the two required* keys, which shipped after it.
correctedState: We implement `requiredMinimumVersion`/`requiredMaximumVersion` (startup refusal, fail-open, enforced in both the desktop shell at apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:1102 and the headless server at packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/headless-start.ts:645) and carry no managed `minimumVersion` key. The gap is cosmetic rather than a real exposure: the updater already has an unconditional, non-overridable floor at the running version, because electron-updater's `allowDowngrade` stays at its default `false` (we never set it and never set `autoUpdater.channel`, the setter that would flip it), so AppUpdater.isUpdateAvailable rejects any feed version older than the installed one. The downgrade path `minimumVersion` guards in Claude -- a /config switch from the `latest` channel to `stable` -- has no analogue here: the update channel is fixed in app-update.yml at build time. A managed `minimumVersion` would only add value if we ever ship a runtime channel switcher or pin-to-version install; until then it would be an admin key that can never change an outcome.
